newsitem.title: USA: Grandmet liquor unit says no U.S. advertising.
newsitem.headline: Grandmet liquor unit says no U.S. advertising.

text.p: Grand Metropolitan Plc's International Distillers and Vintners unit in the United States said it has no plans to begin advertising its liquor products on television unless the industry trade association lifts its voluntary ban on the practice.
"We would not advertise unless or until there is a change in the industry's code of good practices," said a spokesman for Grand Met's liquor unit.
The Distilled Spirits Council of the U.S., which polices the code, has considered reviewing the code and Grand Met supports a change, the spokesman said.

Grand Met labeled as erroneous a report in London's Evening Standard newspaper that it plans to go ahead with a TV ad campaign for its Bailey's Irish Cream brand. It had no comment on other reports that it has investigated the placement of such ads through its agency, Lowe & Partners, an Interpublic unit.
"We would not go ahead and do anything until there is a change in the code," the spokesman said.
"There has been some discussion at the trade association."
